exposure: Maternal weight status (overweight/obese vs. normal weight)
Stage of labor at cesarean section (1st stage vs. 2nd stage)
outcome: Neonatal outcomes (e.g., birth weight, macrosomia, birth asphyxia)
cohort: 636 women with term, singleton pregnancies and cephalic presentation who delivered between January and April 2021
finding: The study found that 5.7% of women had a cesarean section during the second stage of labor, and these women were more likely to be overweight or obese, have excessive gestational weight gain, and have infants with higher birth weight and rates of macrosomia, but experienced no increase in serious adverse outcomes compared to women with first-stage cesarean sections.
mod_finding: Cesarean section during the second stage of labor was associated with higher neonatal birth weight and rates of macrosomia compared to first-stage cesarean sections.
birth_weight: Neonatal birth weight was measured and was higher in infants delivered via second-stage cesarean section.
